intended_object: The vanishing ideal sheaf I_Z of a closed subset Z of a scheme X: the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf whose sections over an affine open U are the f ∈ Γ(X, U) vanishing at every point of Z ∩ U. It is the largest ideal sheaf with support Z (its radical), and its quotient is the reduced induced closed subscheme structure on Z. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition goes through `mkOfMemSupportIff`, which builds an `IdealSheafData`, Mathlib's way of encoding a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf by its ideals on the affine opens. On each affine open U it takes the ideal `PrimeSpectrum.vanishingIdeal (U.2.fromSpec ⁻¹' Z)`. Here `fromSpec` is the open immersion Spec Γ(X, U) → X onto U, so this is exactly the set of sections f ∈ Γ(X, U) that lie in every prime corresponding to a point of Z ∩ U, i.e. that vanish on Z ∩ U.

The proof obligations confirm that this is the right object:
- Compatibility with basic opens: localization commutes with radical vanishing ideals.
- The support is Z: on each affine U, the zero locus of the vanishing ideal is the closure of Z ∩ U in U, which equals Z ∩ U because Z is closed.

This is the standard construction, stated for an arbitrary scheme and an arbitrary closed set. That is its natural generality, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no other definition of this object; this is the Mathlib definition itself.
